fileNodes.name: layout.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Next.js App Router root layout that loads the three Google fonts as CSS variables, declares site-wide SEO/OpenGraph metadata, and wraps every page in the theme provider along with the persistent nav, footer and ambient visual layers.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Uses `next/font/google` to self-host fonts and expose them as CSS custom properties, plus `suppressHydrationWarning` on <html> because the theme class is applied on the client.

fileNodes.name: AmbientBackdrop.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Purely decorative fixed background layer that paints four blurred pastel blobs and a masked dot grid behind all page content, with separate opacities for light and dark mode.
fileNodes.languageNotes: A server component by default (no "use client"), since it holds no state and renders only static markup.

fileNodes.name: CursorGlow.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Client component that renders a soft pastel radial glow which lazily trails the pointer across the page, with separate light and dark gradients, and disables itself for reduced-motion users and non-fine pointers.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Uses Framer Motion's `useMotionValue`/`useSpring`/`useMotionTemplate` so pointer updates drive the gradient without triggering React re-renders.

fileNodes.name: Footer.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Site footer showing the current-year copyright, external links to GitHub, LinkedIn and the hosted résumé, and a playful sign-off line with an animated tilde.

fileNodes.name: Nav.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Fixed, blurred top navigation bar with the wordmark, four route links whose active item is highlighted by a shared-layout animated pill, the theme toggle, and the scroll progress hairline.
fileNodes.languageNotes: The active-link pill uses Framer Motion's `layoutId` so the highlight animates smoothly between routes instead of re-mounting.

fileNodes.name: ScrollProgress.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Two-pixel gradient bar pinned to the bottom edge of the nav that scales horizontally with the page's scroll progress, smoothed by a spring.

fileNodes.name: ThemeProvider.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Custom theme layer that owns an auto/light/dark preference persisted to localStorage, re-evaluates the clock-scheduled theme on a timer and on tab visibility changes, and feeds the resolved theme into next-themes as a forced theme.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Wraps next-themes with `forcedTheme` and `enableSystem: false`, so this provider — not the OS setting — is the single source of truth; `useLayoutEffect` reads localStorage before paint to limit theme flash.

fileNodes.name: ThemeToggle.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Round sun/moon button in the nav that pins light or dark on click and returns to clock-scheduled auto mode on Alt+click, rendering a neutral placeholder until the theme preference has hydrated.

fileNodes.name: scheduledTheme.ts
fileNodes.summary: Single-function module encoding the site's time-of-day theme schedule: light between 06:00 and 19:00 local time, dark otherwise.

fileNodes.name: utils.ts
fileNodes.summary: Shared class-name helper module exposing the `cn` utility used across every component for conditional Tailwind styling.

fileNodes.name: page.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Next.js App Router route for /contact, rendering a mailto card plus magnetic GitHub, LinkedIn and résumé links wrapped in scroll reveal animations.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Server component (no "use client") that exports a static `metadata` object for the route title while still composing client-only motion primitives as children.

fileNodes.name: page.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Home page of the portfolio, composing the animated hero (rotating greeting, split headline, tilting portrait), a two-project 'Selected work' grid and the GitHub contribution graph.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Client component that spreads a shared `fade` variant object into multiple `motion.p` elements and uses `next/image` with explicit `sizes` for responsive art direction.

fileNodes.name: ContributionGraph.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Renders the author's last-year GitHub contribution calendar in the site's lilac palette, scaling the fixed-width calendar to exactly fill its container.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Uses `useLayoutEffect` with a `ResizeObserver` to measure the calendar's natural width before paint, then applies a CSS transform scale so the third-party widget stretches without a gutter.

fileNodes.name: HeroPortrait.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Hero photo card with offset pastel backing layers and a cursor-tracked radial shine highlight that springs toward the pointer on hover.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Combines Framer Motion `useMotionValue`/`useSpring` with `useMotionTemplate` to build a CSS radial-gradient string that updates without React re-renders.

fileNodes.name: RotatingHi.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Small hero greeting that cycles through four intro lines every 4.2 seconds with an animated enter/exit transition.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Uses `AnimatePresence mode="wait"` keyed on the line text so the outgoing phrase finishes exiting before the next enters; `aria-live="polite"` announces changes.

fileNodes.name: Magnetic.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Reusable motion primitive that makes its children drift toward the cursor while hovered and spring back on leave, used for buttons and pill links across the site.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Respects `useReducedMotion` by short-circuiting the pointer handler, so the wrapper stays inert for users who prefer reduced motion.

fileNodes.name: Reveal.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Reusable scroll-reveal primitive that fades and lifts its children into place as they enter the viewport; the most widely reused animation wrapper in the site.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Uses Framer Motion's `whileInView` with a negative viewport margin and an `once` flag, and drops the y-offset entirely under reduced-motion preferences.

fileNodes.name: SplitHeadline.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Headline primitive that splits text into individual characters and staggers each one rising into place, with a per-letter hover lift.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Splits with `Array.from` for correct code-point handling and hides the per-character spans from assistive tech via `aria-hidden`, exposing the full string through `aria-label` instead.

fileNodes.name: page.tsx
fileNodes.summary: App Router page for the /projects route that renders every entry from the shared projects content module as a responsive two-column grid of image-led cards with tech-stack stickers and external links. Composes the Reveal, TiltCard and WavyRule motion primitives around otherwise static server-rendered markup.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Next.js App Router server component: it exports a `metadata` object for per-route SEO and stays server-rendered while delegating all interactivity to the imported "use client" motion wrappers.

fileNodes.name: WavyRule.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Client component providing a decorative horizontal divider drawn as a soft SVG wave that animates its stroke into view on scroll. Used as a section separator across the home, contact, experience and projects pages.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Uses framer-motion's `pathLength` with `whileInView` and `viewport.once` so the stroke draws itself exactly once; `useReducedMotion` short-circuits to a fully drawn path for accessibility.

fileNodes.name: TiltCard.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Client-side motion wrapper that applies a subtle spring-damped 3D tilt to its children as the cursor moves across them. Used to add depth to project and experience cards.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Drives rotation through framer-motion `useMotionValue` piped into `useSpring`, keeping the tilt off the React render path so pointer moves never trigger re-renders.

fileNodes.name: projects.ts
fileNodes.summary: Single source of truth for portfolio project entries, exporting a typed `Project[]` array with name, period, subtitle, description, cover image, tech stack and external links for each project. Consumed by both the projects page and the home page.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Content-as-code pattern: the `Project` and `ProjectLink` types are declared alongside the data and the array is annotated `Project[]`, so schema drift in any entry surfaces as a compile-time error rather than a runtime render bug.

fileNodes.name: page.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Next.js App Router server page for the /experience route that renders the career timeline by mapping over the typed `roles` content array into logo, title, date-range and highlight cards. Composes WavyRule, Reveal and TimelineProgress with a rotating pastel dot palette for each timeline entry.
fileNodes.languageNotes: A Next.js App Router page: the exported `metadata` object supplies the route title, and the default export is a server component that renders no client hooks itself — interactivity is delegated to the imported client components.

fileNodes.name: TimelineProgress.tsx
fileNodes.summary: Client component providing the vertical timeline rail that fills with an accent gradient as the user scrolls past the role list it sits beside. Respects the user's reduced-motion preference by omitting the animated fill entirely.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Uses framer-motion's `useScroll` with an element target and offset window, smoothed through `useSpring`, to drive a CSS `scaleY` transform rather than re-rendering on every scroll frame.

fileNodes.name: experience.ts
fileNodes.summary: Typed content module defining the `Role` shape and exporting the `roles` array — the newest-first list of jobs with company, location, date range, summary, highlight bullets and logo path — that drives the experience timeline UI.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Content-as-code pattern: a plain TypeScript module annotated with an exported `Role` type gives the page compile-time safety over the data without a CMS or runtime validation layer.

fileNodes.name: next-env.d.ts
fileNodes.summary: Auto-generated Next.js ambient type declaration file that pulls in the `next` and `next/image-types/global` type references so TypeScript understands framework globals and image imports. Not meant to be hand-edited.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Triple-slash `/// <reference types="..." />` directives are the TypeScript mechanism for injecting ambient declarations without an import statement.

fileNodes.name: next.config.mjs
fileNodes.summary: Next.js framework configuration that tunes the built-in image optimizer, preferring WebP over AVIF (AVIF softens JPEG portraits at default quality) and declaring a custom device-size breakpoint ladder up to 3840px.
fileNodes.languageNotes: The `/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */` JSDoc annotation gives a plain `.mjs` file full TypeScript autocompletion and checking without converting it to TypeScript.

fileNodes.name: package.json
fileNodes.summary: Package manifest for the private `anuraag-web` portfolio, declaring the standard Next.js dev/build/start/lint scripts and pinning the runtime stack: Next 14.2, React 18, framer-motion, next-themes, lucide-react, react-github-calendar and the Tailwind class utilities (clsx, tailwind-merge).

fileNodes.name: postcss.config.mjs
fileNodes.summary: Minimal PostCSS configuration registering Tailwind CSS as the sole plugin, which is what expands the `@tailwind` directives and `@apply` rules in the global stylesheet during the build.

fileNodes.name: globals.css
fileNodes.summary: Global stylesheet that loads the three Tailwind layers and defines the site's light/dark design tokens as raw RGB channel triples (`--tw-canvas`, `--tw-ink`, `--tw-line`, ...) on `:root` and `.dark`. Also supplies the decorative `.grain` SVG-noise and `.wash` gradient overlays, wavy-underline treatment, custom selection colors and theming for the GitHub contribution-calendar tooltips.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Storing colors as space-separated RGB channels (`45 42 51`) rather than full `rgb()` values is what lets Tailwind's `<alpha-value>` placeholder compose opacity modifiers like `bg-canvas/50` on top of CSS-variable-driven themes.

fileNodes.name: template.tsx
fileNodes.summary: App Router `template.tsx` client component that wraps every routed page in a framer-motion fade-and-rise transition. Unlike a layout, a template remounts on each navigation, so the animation replays on every route change.
fileNodes.languageNotes: In the Next.js App Router, `layout.tsx` persists across navigations while `template.tsx` creates a fresh instance per route — the standard place to hang enter animations.

fileNodes.name: tailwind.config.ts
fileNodes.summary: Tailwind design-system configuration: enables class-based dark mode, scopes content scanning to src/app, src/components and src/pages, and extends the theme with CSS-variable-backed semantic colors (canvas, surface, ink, line), a pastel and accent palette, three font families, soft/card/lift shadows, and float/wiggle keyframe animations.
fileNodes.languageNotes: Typing the export as `Config` from `tailwindcss` gives compile-time validation of the whole theme object; the `rgb(var(--token) / <alpha-value>)` pattern bridges CSS custom properties into Tailwind's opacity modifier system.

fileNodes.name: tsconfig.json
fileNodes.summary: TypeScript compiler configuration for the Next.js project: strict mode with `noEmit` (Next handles transpilation), bundler module resolution, preserved JSX, incremental builds, the `next` language-service plugin, and the `@/*` path alias mapping to `./src/*`.
